text: Good API design follows several key practices. First, REST APIs should use clear and meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers can easily understand what each one does. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Third, write clear documentation so others know how to use your API without guessing. Finally, use versioning, for example /api/v1/users, to keep old versions working when you make changes. Following these practices makes your API easier to use, maintain, and improve over time.
